question.worked_solution:
The variable $z$ is being *multiplied* by $-2.$ To isolate $z,$ we perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $-2.$ Remember to perform the same operation on both sides.

Also, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2z\,\, & <\,\,7 \\ \frac{-2z}{-2}\,\, & >\,\,\frac{7}{-2} \\ \frac{-2z}{-2}\,\, & >\,\,-\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $-2$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-2z}{-2} & >-\frac{7}{2} \\ \frac{\cancel{-2}z}{\cancel{-2}} & >-\frac{7}{2} \\ z & >-\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $z>-\frac{7}{2}.$
